messages:
kevin: Heads up — nightly perf run shows a 6-10% CPU tail on host for small-seq (<=64) requests. Flame points at token preproc + request parse path.
clara: Oof. Is this the new batching heuristic change from yesterday?
kevin: Not directly. I bisected; the regression lands when we switched the framing to incremental chunking + the new HTTP header parsing micro-op.
sam: Can you paste the flame or pprof snippet?
kevin: Sure, quick snapshot from pprof CPU (top 5):
```
60.2%  host_tokenize
18.9%  request_parse_frame
7.4%   stream_coalesce
5.1%   http2_writev
3.4%   kvcache_lookup_hot
```
kevin: Tokenize is doing many small allocs and doing UTF8 validation per char; request_parse_frame is copying headers into a temp buffer on every chunk.
elle: @kevin did we enable `--incremental-frag` only for grpc paths? Might be hitting http as well.
kevin: We flipped it for both to simplify routing. Looks like http path has worse syscall churn.
clara: Reaction: :thinking_face: Could we short-circuit tokenization for ascii-only inputs (fast path) and skip extra allocations?
sam: We already had ascii fast-path in rust-proxy but host-side is C++ shim; not implemented. I can prototype a branch to avoid per-char checks and use a memchr-based scan.
kevin: That + avoid header-copy by parsing in-place should cut ~4-6% CPU. Also thinking KV cache lookups are serialized behind a mutex when fragmenting — add try_lock fast path to avoid stall on hot keys.
perf-bot: New flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.internal/fg/1822223333 (contains full stack + sample rates)
elle: Good. Can we canary a build that re-enables incremental chunking but with token fast-path and in-place header parse?
kevin: Plan: sam will push proto with token fast-path + in-place parsing in a PR, we'll run a canary on canary-2 (10% traffic) tomorrow morning. If tail reduces to <2%, we roll forward.
clara: Add an e2e with synthetic ascii-only payload and mixed utf8 to catch regressions. Also add perf regression alert on host-cpu-tail >= 4%.
sam: Will open PR and attach microbench results. ETA tomorrow AM.
kevin: Thanks. If anyone sees kvcache spikes in the meantime, @sam or I will look.
elle: :thumbsup:
